title: Chapter 132 — Returns, Exchanges & Refunds
intro: A return is not a lost sale — it is a second chance to sell.

sections.title: The Return Conversation
sections.content:
Do not ask 'what is wrong with it?' Ask 'what happened — tell me about it.' Listen without defending the product or the sale. Acknowledge: 'I understand. That is not the experience we want you to have.' Solve: offer the solution before they demand it.

Process the return first, sell second. Never hold a return hostage to a new sale. If you handle the return with grace, they will often buy again in the same visit without you asking.

sections.title: Turning Returns Into Exchanges
sections.content:
Buyer's remorse: 'No problem at all. Let me process the return and if you want, we can look at what might be a better fit. Sometimes seeing it in your kitchen changes what you thought you wanted — that is completely normal.'

Wrong product: 'Let us fix this. I will set up the exchange for the right model. If there is a price difference, I will make sure you get today's pricing on the new one.'

The exchange is usually a step-up opportunity. The customer who returned the 300 series may be ready for the 500 series now that they understand what they actually need.

sections.title: Tracking Returns
sections.content:
Log every return with the reason. Patterns tell you if a product has issues, if a rep is misselling, or if your discovery process is failing on a specific category.

Return rate above 8 percent is a red flag. Below 4 percent is excellent. Between 4-8 percent is normal for appliance retail. Know your number and investigate the outliers.
